correctness.rationale: For biregular graph A-degree r and B-degree s, class-constant relative phase reduces exactly to u->u-(r+s)h sin u. Existence and uniqueness of ±a follows strict monotonicity of 2a/sin a. Bipartite Perron–Frobenius gives Lambda=lambda_max=r+s simple. At both points cosine=-cos(a), so return derivative is (I-h cos(a)L)^2 and multipliers (1-2a cot(a) lambda_j/Lambda)^2. Since q=2a cot(a) decreases from 2 to negative, every transverse multiplier <1 iff 2/Lambda<h<pi/Lambda and >1 above. Convex spectral maximum occurs at lambda_2 or Lambda; balancing opposite-sign endpoint factors yields unique minimizer rho=[(Lambda-lambda2)/(Lambda+lambda2)]². The upper boundary parabolic computation is explicitly restricted to invariant two-colour manifold, m x_m² ->1/pi². Independent finite matrix/eigenvalue checks on stars and bicliques corroborate optimal radii.
residual_risks: All return multipliers equal one at h=pi/Lambda; nonlinear transverse stability is not established there.
No global attraction basin or all-cycle uniqueness beyond the two-colour ansatz.
